title: Singular partitive of common -as/-äs words
summary: For these -as/-äs words, keep the base consonants and add -ta/-tä: vieras (“guest”) → vierasta.
objectives: Form the singular partitive in this bounded word family.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: A case is a word form used for a grammatical job. The dictionary form is the form used to look up a word. The partitive has several uses; it does not always mean “some”. Here you practise forming the word, so no sentence construction is required.

For these selected -as/-äs words, add -ta/-tä to the unchanged dictionary form. Keep the consonants visible in the base: singular hammasta keeps mm and singular opasta keeps one p. The selected words belong to the family whose plural is taught next; not every word ending in -as/-äs has the same plural stem.
keyPoints: Learn each word with its pattern; a similar final letter does not guarantee the same stem.

steps: Keep vieras and add -ta: vieras → vierasta.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “guest”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Keep mm and add -ta to hammas: hammas → hammasta.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “tooth”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Keep varas and add -ta: varas → varasta.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “thief”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Keep one p and add -ta: saapas → saapasta.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “boot”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Keep one p and add -ta: opas → opasta.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “guide”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Keep one k and add -ta: rakas → rakasta.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “dear”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Keep one k and add -ta: rikas → rikasta.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “rich”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.
Keep one k and add -tä: älykäs → älykästä.
The word’s meaning stays connected to “intelligent”; its singular case form changes its grammatical use.

commonMistakes: Keep the dictionary consonants in the singular partitive.
Do not use the strengthened plural stem here.
